flow_ref: User story (not in any OCMS flow deck)
code_summary: ocmsadminprivateapi crud/ocmsizdb/OcmsValidOffenceNotice/OcmsValidOffenceNoticeRepository (findToppanNoticesForStage), framework/workflows/agencies/toppan/upload/{helpers/ToppanUploadHelper (resolveStageContext, bulkUpdateVonStage), jobs/ToppanUploadJob, models/ToppanStage}, framework/schedulers/ToppanUploadJobsScheduler, framework/controllers/ToppanUnifiedController, properties cron-schedules-prod and application-prod. ocmsadminapi crud/ocmsizdb/OcmsChangeOfProcessing/{ChangeOfProcessingController, ChangeOfProcessingService} (manual stage change by staff), workflows/cas_integration/service/CasIntegrationServiceImpl. ocmsadminui, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi: no related code
note: Status 'Requirement given - Gen flow'; demo_remark 'Removed from demo list. Unable to verify.' (not 'User Story Removed', so traced normally). No flow deck. The story asks OCMS to escalate the notice to the court processing stage against the driver using the Appendix D conditions of Annex 1A. The text 'Appendix D' / 'Annex 1A' does not appear in the six repos (case-insensitive grep, 0 hits) and there is no court-condition rule engine (grep 'offence history', 'repeat offence', 'charge in court', 'prosecut', 'summons' in the APIs: 0 relevant hits). What exists: after the DR3 letter is processed, ToppanUploadHelper fills next_processing_stage = CPC (from ocms_stage_map, hardcoded fallback 'CPC') and next_processing_date in VON/eVON; but no job later processes next_processing_stage = CPC because ToppanStage only has RD1-DR3 and ANL. Getting into CPC (last_processing_stage = CPC) is only possible through the manual staff change-processing-stage feature in ocmsadminapi (which also adds a surcharge, OCMS-SR-2026-107) or an update from CAS. The DR3 letter itself in prod only runs through the manual trigger because the executeJob call in the scheduler is commented out (ToppanUploadJobsScheduler.java:118), and the stage advances without delivery because sftp.upload.disabledServers=toppan (OCMS-DF-2026-192, status Ready to UAT). Whether CPC = the 'court processing stage' in Appendix D cannot be confirmed from the repo (SystemConstant puts CPC in COURT_STAGES_SURCHARGE but not in COURT_STAGES). The ocms_stage_map rows and the STAGEDAYS parameter live in the DB, cannot verify from repo. Story OCMS12.36 (composition vs court decision) also has no code for the 'count of offence history' condition; the escalation here depends on that decision.
recommendation: Do not claim as done. Only setting next stage CPC after the DR3 letter and the manual stage change by staff exist; the Appendix D conditions and automatic move to the court stage do not. Ask URA/the team where the court decision and escalation were built, or mark as a gap

steps.step: Driver notices at stage DR3 that are due, not suspended and not Advisory Notices are picked for processing to the next stage
steps.detail: findToppanNoticesForStage('DR3') selects von.next_processing_stage = :stage, next_processing_date <= today, suspension_type IS NULL, an_flag not 'Y', for the current offender (offender_indicator = 'Y') (OcmsValidOffenceNoticeRepository.java:583-614). That is the DR3 letter batch pick-up (ToppanUploadJob accepts stages RD1-DR3, TJ:136-142), not an evaluation of the 'decision to charge the driver in court'. The criteria are only date and suspension status; there is no check of offence history, count or Appendix D conditions. Hence Sebagian: the right notices are picked, but not through the pre-defined conditions named in the story.

steps.step: OCMS assesses the pre-defined conditions (Appendix D of Annex 1A) to decide to take the driver to court
steps.detail: No rule, parameter or method evaluates court conditions. 'Appendix D' / 'Annex 1A' does not appear in the six repos, and a synonym search (offence history, repeat offence, charge in court, prosecut, summons) in ocmsadminapi, ocmsadminprivateapi, thirdpartyapi, ocmseserviceapi found no decision logic. The only 'decision' after DR3 is resolveStageContext, which takes the next stage from ocms_stage_map without any condition (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1813-1824) and computes the date from STAGEDAYS (:1368-1370). The content of Appendix D itself is not in the repo, cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: After the DR3 processing, the notice is scheduled to the court processing stage (next stage = CPC with its date)
steps.detail: After the DR3 letter, resolveStageContext takes the next stage from ocms_stage_map and, if empty, uses the fallback 'CPC' for RR3/DR3 (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1813-1820). bulkUpdateVonStage then writes last_processing_stage = DR3, next_processing_stage = CPC, next_processing_date = processing date + STAGEDAYS to VON (:1368-1370, 1418-1421) and the same next stage to the eVON payload (:1435). Limits: (1) the ocms_stage_map content and STAGEDAYS live in the DB, cannot verify from repo; (2) in prod the call toppanLettersGeneratorService.executeJob() in the scheduler is commented out (ToppanUploadJobsScheduler.java:118), so it only runs through the manual trigger POST /toppan/generate-letters (ToppanUnifiedController.java:34); (3) sftp.upload.disabledServers=toppan (application-prod.properties:86) makes the stage advance without delivery confirmation (OCMS-DF-2026-192, Ready to UAT). This is scheduling, not a move into the court stage.

steps.step: The notice actually enters the court processing stage (last_processing_stage = CPC) automatically
steps.detail: No job processes next_processing_stage = CPC: the ToppanStage enum only has RD1, RD2, RR3, DN1, DN2, DR3, ANL (ToppanStage.java:20-26) and ToppanUploadJob rejects other stages (ToppanUploadJob.java:138-142). What sets last_processing_stage = CPC is the manual staff feature POST /change-processing-stage (ChangeOfProcessingController.java:47) through ChangeOfProcessingService: CPC is in ELIGIBLE_STAGES (:64-66), it recalculates amount payable and surcharge for CPC (:999-1030; OCMS-SR-2026-107), then updateVonStage writes last = the new stage (:1093-1110). CasIntegrationServiceImpl also passes through whatever stage CAS sends (:437-439); the CAS side cannot be verified from repo. So escalation to court exists as a manual action or from another system, not automatically by OCMS as the story says. The code also treats CPC as non-court (SuspensionBaseHelper.java:167 in ocmsadminprivateapi), so it is not certain that 'court processing stage' = CPC.
